review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

5:1.sourceText: Περὶ δὲ τῶν χρόνων καὶ τῶν καιρῶν, ἀδελφοί, οὐ χρείαν ἔχετε ὑμῖν γράφεσθαι·
5:1.targetText: And concerning the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need of my writing to you,

groups.note: The Greek passive infinitive γράφεσθαι, for this to be written to you, is recast as English of my writing to you. The writing predicate remains shared, while the English agentive possessive my is separately noted as supplied.

unmappedTarget.reason: English writer possessive is supplied: Greek has no ἐμοῦ or other my with writing here.

5:2.sourceText: αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἀκριβῶς οἴδατε ὅτι ἡμέρα Κυρίου ὡς κλέπτης ἐν νυκτὶ οὕτως ἔρχεται.
5:2.targetText: for you have thoroughly known that the Day of the LORD so comes as a thief in the night,

5:3.sourceText: ὅταν λέγωσιν Εἰρήνη καὶ ἀσφάλεια, τότε αἰφνίδιος αὐτοῖς ἐπίσταται ὄλεθρος ὥσπερ ἡ ὠδὶν τῇ ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσῃ, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἐκφύγωσιν.
5:3.targetText: for when they may say, “Peace and security,” then sudden destruction comes [on] them, as the travail [on] her who is with child, and they will not escape;

groups.note: The dative recipient αὐτοῖς is expressed as [on] them, including an English preposition for its case relation.
The dative feminine substantival article τῇ identifies the woman on whom travail comes; English renders its case and substantival/relative function as [on] her who.
The Greek idiom ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσῃ, having in the womb, means being pregnant and is rendered is with child. Child is not falsely equated with the isolated Greek noun womb; the whole idiom is retained.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness difference: LSV follows the additional TR γάρ before when; N1904 starts with ὅταν.

5:4.sourceText: ὑμεῖς δέ, ἀδελφοί, οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐν σκότει, ἵνα ἡ ἡμέρα ὑμᾶς ὡς κλέπτης καταλάβῃ·
5:4.targetText: but you, brothers, are not in darkness, that the Day may catch you as a thief;

5:5.sourceText: πάντες γὰρ ὑμεῖς υἱοὶ φωτός ἐστε καὶ υἱοὶ ἡμέρας. Οὐκ ἐσμὲν νυκτὸς οὐδὲ σκότους·
5:5.targetText: you are all sons of light, and sons of day; we are not of night, nor of darkness,

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness difference: N1904 has explanatory γάρ here, absent from TR and LSV.

5:6.sourceText: ἄρα οὖν μὴ καθεύδωμεν ὡς οἱ λοιποί, ἀλλὰ γρηγορῶμεν καὶ νήφωμεν.
5:6.targetText: so, then, we may not sleep as also the others, but watch and be sober,

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness difference: LSV also follows TR καί in ὡς καὶ οἱ λοιποί, whereas N1904 has ὡς οἱ λοιποί.

5:7.sourceText: οἱ γὰρ καθεύδοντες νυκτὸς καθεύδουσιν, καὶ οἱ μεθυσκόμενοι νυκτὸς μεθύουσιν·
5:7.targetText: for those sleeping, sleep by night, and those making themselves drunk, are drunken by night,

5:8.sourceText: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἡμέρας ὄντες νήφωμεν, ἐνδυσάμενοι θώρακα πίστεως καὶ ἀγάπης καὶ περικεφαλαίαν ἐλπίδα σωτηρίας·
5:8.targetText: and we, being of the day—let us be sober, putting on a breastplate of faith and love, and a helmet—a hope of salvation,

5:9.sourceText: ὅτι οὐκ ἔθετο ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς εἰς ὀργὴν ἀλλὰ εἰς περιποίησιν σωτηρίας διὰ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
5:9.targetText: because God did not appoint us to anger, but to the acquiring of salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,

5:10.sourceText: τοῦ ἀποθανόντος περὶ ἡμῶν, ἵνα εἴτε γρηγορῶμεν εἴτε καθεύδωμεν ἅμα σὺν αὐτῷ ζήσωμεν.
5:10.targetText: who died for us, that whether we wake—whether we sleep—we may live together with Him;

groups.note: N1904 περί with the genitive, here on behalf of us, is rendered for us. TR instead has ὑπέρ; the contextual relation is shared without claiming identical preposition readings.

5:11.sourceText: Διὸ παρακαλεῖτε ἀλλήλους καὶ οἰκοδομεῖτε εἷς τὸν ἕνα, καθὼς καὶ ποιεῖτε.
5:11.targetText: for this reason, comfort one another, and build up one another, as also you do.

groups.note: The Greek reciprocal expression εἷς τὸν ἕνα, one [building up] the other, is rendered as the whole English reciprocal one another.

5:12.sourceText: Ἐρωτῶμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, εἰδέναι τοὺς κοπιῶντας ἐν ὑμῖν καὶ προϊσταμένους ὑμῶν ἐν Κυρίῳ καὶ νουθετοῦντας ὑμᾶς,
5:12.targetText: And we ask you, brothers, to know those laboring among you and leading you in the LORD and admonishing you,

5:13.sourceText: καὶ ἡγεῖσθαι αὐτοὺς ὑπερεκπερισσῶς ἐν ἀγάπῃ διὰ τὸ ἔργον αὐτῶν. εἰρηνεύετε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς.
5:13.targetText: and to esteem them very abundantly in love, because of their work; be at peace among yourselves;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

5:14.sourceText: Παρακαλοῦμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, νουθετεῖτε τοὺς ἀτάκτους, παραμυθεῖσθε τοὺς ὀλιγοψύχους, ἀντέχεσθε τῶν ἀσθενῶν, μακροθυμεῖτε πρὸς πάντας.
5:14.targetText: and we exhort you, brothers, admonish the disorderly, comfort the feeble-minded, support the weak, be patient to all;

5:15.sourceText: ὁρᾶτε μή τις κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ τινι ἀποδῷ, ἀλλὰ πάντοτε τὸ ἀγαθὸν διώκετε εἰς ἀλλήλους καὶ εἰς πάντας.
5:15.targetText: see [that] no one may render evil for evil to anyone, but always pursue that which is good, both to one another and to all;

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English complementizer supplies the see that construction; Greek has no separate ὅτι or ἵνα here.
Source-witness difference: LSV both follows the first TR καί before εἰς ἀλλήλους; that conjunction is absent in N1904, whose actual later καί remains linked to and.

5:18.sourceText: ἐν παντὶ εὐχαριστεῖτε· τοῦτο γὰρ θέλημα Θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ εἰς ὑμᾶς.
5:18.targetText: give thanks in everything, for this [is] the will of God in Christ Jesus in regard to you.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

5:21.sourceText: πάντα δὲ δοκιμάζετε, τὸ καλὸν κατέχετε·
5:21.targetText: prove all things; hold fast [to] that which is good;

groups.note: The substantivized adjective τὸ καλόν means the good/what is good, rendered that which is good as one nominal constituent.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness difference: N1904 δέ is absent from TR and is not separately rendered by LSV.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English preposition completes hold fast to; Greek κατέχετε directly governs the accusative good without a separate preposition.

5:22.targetText: abstain from all appearance of evil;

5:23.sourceText: Αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ Θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης ἁγιάσαι ὑμᾶς ὁλοτελεῖς, καὶ ὁλόκληρον ὑμῶν τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ ἡ ψυχὴ καὶ τὸ σῶμα ἀμέμπτως ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τηρηθείη.
5:23.targetText: and may the God of peace Himself sanctify you wholly, and may your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved, unblameably at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ;

groups.note: The aorist optative ἁγιάσαι is a wish, rendered may sanctify; may is part of that mood, not a separate Greek permission verb.
The passive optative τηρηθείη is the coordinated wish rendered may ... be preserved.

5:24.targetText: He who is calling you is steadfast, who also will do [it].

5:26.sourceText: Ἀσπάσασθε τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς πάντας ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ.
5:26.targetText: Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.

5:27.sourceText: Ἐνορκίζω ὑμᾶς τὸν Κύριον ἀναγνωσθῆναι τὴν ἐπιστολὴν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς.
5:27.targetText: I charge you [by] the LORD, that the letter be read to all the holy brothers.

groups.note: N1904 uses the oath-charging compound ἐνορκίζω, whereas TR has ὁρκίζω. Both support the LSV I charge rendering in the explicit Lord-as-oath-witness construction.
The accusative oath-witness τὸν Κύριον with charge is rendered [by] the LORD. The bracketed English preposition expresses the function of the whole Greek noun phrase.
The passive infinitive ἀναγνωσθῆναι is rendered as a content clause that the letter be read; that is part of this English clausal conversion.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness difference: LSV holy follows the TR adjective ἁγίοις before brothers, absent in N1904.
